launches.title: Hemlock: The missing force signal in robotic training data
launches.tagline: We collect egocentric video data + force and contact dynamics derived from workers' muscular signals. Adding Hemlock's force data to human training demos improved pi0.5's success by 10x and Gemini Argon's by 2.7x on force-sensitive manipulation tasks.
launches.body:
## TL;DR:

**For robots to be effective, they need to understand real world force and contact dynamics.**

We equip workers with EMG wearables and egocentric video gear to analyze their muscular signals and generate the force/contact data needed to **train physical AI models to use their hands the same way skilled workers do**. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124952&key=user_uploads/2947535/4f8a50ae-f121-473e-a450-1d2a5726b1cd)

Adding Hemlock's force data to human training demos **improved Pi0.5's success** **on egg pick-and-place by** **10x** and **Gemini 4 Argon's success** **on a lightbulb screwing task by** **2.7x**. If you or anybody you know is working on robotic dexterous manipulation or training physical AI models, [**please get in touch ASAP :)**](mailto:julian@hemlock.inc)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124952&key=user_uploads/2947535/33e3ff55-81e7-402f-80fb-fadf63fa0317)

## **The Problem 🤖**

Today’s robotics companies and frontier physical AI model labs are spending **hundreds of millions** on egocentric video data to train their systems to perform tasks in place of humans. However, whether the deployment site is somebody’s kitchen or an automotive assembly line, successful task execution depends on an understanding of force and contact dynamics. 

**Currently, there’s no good way to get this data into a model.**

1. Tactile gloves occlude the user’s hands. 
2. Instrumenting the environment isn’t scalable. 
3. Video alone drops this information entirely.

And thus, Hemlock was born.

<https://youtu.be/adox0I2cmBE>

## Hemlock - The Missing Piece 🧩

Hemlock equips skilled workers with egocentric video capture gear and our proprietary EMG wearable - the Bracelet. We read their muscular activity while they do their day-to-day work to understand how they apply force with their fingers, move their hands, and manipulate objects and tools. 

We turn a day of work into rich tactile information used to improve robotic AI models’ dexterous manipulation capabilities. Any industry. Any task.

We recently collected a few minutes of human demonstration data on a basic egg pick-and-place task, using it to finetune **Pi0.5** twice: **once only with video and once with video + Bracelet data**. 

Success rates shot up **10x**.

We then decided to up the ante: same idea, except screwing in a lightbulb using **a humanoid hand** and **Google’s Gemini 4 Argon model**.

Up **2.7x**.

Check out the full videos [here](https://hemlock.inc/#case-study) ;)

## The Ask ⁉️

1. **working on physical AI foundation models,**
2. **involved in data ops at robotics/physical AI companies,**
3. **working on robotic manipulation,**
4. **automating a force-sensitive task for a deployment,**
5. **friends with anybody fitting the criteria above,**

   **please [shoot me an email](mailto:julian@hemlock.inc). I’d love to discuss your data needs and any intros would be greatly appreciated 🙏**
